userStories.title: Extract Shared Auth Config and Harden JWT Secret
userStories.description: The JWT signing secret is duplicated in lib/auth.ts and middleware.ts with an identical hardcoded fallback string. Extract to a shared module and fail loudly if AUTH_SECRET is missing in production.
acceptanceCriteria: Create lib/config.ts exporting SECRET_KEY (TextEncoder-encoded AUTH_SECRET)
lib/config.ts throws an error if AUTH_SECRET env var is missing when NODE_ENV === 'production'
lib/config.ts allows the fallback only when NODE_ENV !== 'production' (for local dev)
lib/auth.ts imports SECRET_KEY from lib/config.ts instead of constructing its own
middleware.ts imports SECRET_KEY from lib/config.ts instead of constructing its own
No duplicate secret construction remains in the codebase
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Currently both files have: const SECRET_KEY = new TextEncoder().encode(process.env.AUTH_SECRET || 'fallback-secret-change-in-production'). This is a duplication risk and a production safety issue.

userStories.title: Add Error Handling to Unprotected API Routes
userStories.description: Three API routes lack try-catch blocks, meaning a DB failure would return an unhandled 500 with a stack trace instead of a clean error response.
acceptanceCriteria: app/api/auth/logout/route.ts: wrap deleteSession() call in try-catch, return 500 JSON on failure
app/api/auth/me/route.ts: wrap getCurrentUser() call in try-catch, return 500 JSON on failure
app/api/activity/route.ts: wrap the entire GET handler body in try-catch, return 500 JSON on failure with console.error
Error responses follow existing pattern: { error: 'descriptive message' } with status 500
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: All other API routes in the codebase use try-catch consistently. These three are the exceptions. Match the pattern used in e.g. app/api/menus/route.ts.

userStories.title: Validate PDF Magic Bytes on Upload
userStories.description: The version upload endpoint at app/api/menus/[id]/versions/route.ts only checks file.type (MIME type), which is client-controlled. Add server-side validation of the actual file content by checking the PDF magic bytes.
acceptanceCriteria: After the existing MIME type check, read the first 5 bytes of the uploaded file buffer
Verify the file starts with the PDF signature bytes: %PDF- (hex: 25 50 44 46 2D)
If magic bytes don't match, return 400 with error 'File is not a valid PDF'
The existing MIME type check remains in place as a fast first check
The file buffer is read only once (reuse for both validation and upload)
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Currently at line 55: if (!file || file.type !== 'application/pdf'). A malicious client can set any MIME type. The file.arrayBuffer() is already called later in lib/blob.ts uploadPdf, but we need to check bytes before passing to upload.

userStories.title: Validate Annotation Data Shape
userStories.description: The annotation POST and PATCH endpoints only check typeof data === 'object' but don't validate the internal structure. Add runtime validation against the AnnotationData types defined in lib/annotation-types.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: Create a validateAnnotationData(tool, data) function in lib/annotation-types.ts that returns { valid: boolean; error?: string }
For pen: data must have type 'pen', points array (each with numeric x and y in 0-1 range), numeric strokeWidth > 0
For text: data must have type 'text', numeric x and y in 0-1 range, non-empty string content (max 500 chars), numeric fontSize > 0
For checkmark: data must have type 'checkmark', numeric x and y in 0-1 range, numeric size > 0
For highlight: data must have type 'highlight', numeric x and y in 0-1 range, numeric width > 0 and height > 0
POST handler in app/api/versions/[id]/annotations/route.ts calls validateAnnotationData after the existing typeof check
PATCH handler in same file calls validateAnnotationData when data is provided
Invalid data returns 400 with the specific validation error message
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Type definitions already exist in lib/annotation-types.ts (PenData, TextData, CheckmarkData, HighlightData). Coordinates are normalized to 0-1 range by the canvas component. The tool field is already validated against the enum; this adds shape validation for the data field.

userStories.title: Add Database Indexes for Query Performance
userStories.description: The schema has no indexes beyond primary keys. Add indexes to foreign key columns and columns used in WHERE/ORDER BY clauses across API routes.
acceptanceCriteria: Add index on versions.menuId (used in dashboard subqueries, version list, export)
Add index on versions.status (used in dashboard 'needs attention' subquery)
Add index on versions.assignedTo (used in dashboard assigned-version check)
Add index on comments.versionId (used in comments list query)
Add index on activityLogs.userId (used in activity log queries)
Add index on activityLogs.createdAt (used in ORDER BY for activity list and export)
Add index on annotations.versionId (used in annotation GET queries)
Add composite index on menuTags(menuId, tagId) (used in batch tag fetching)
All indexes added in lib/db/schema.ts using Drizzle's index() function
Run bun run db:generate to create migration, then bun run db:push to apply
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Drizzle ORM supports indexes via pgTable's third argument or .indexes(). Use the pattern: (table) => ({ menuIdIdx: index('idx_versions_menu_id').on(table.menuId) }). See Drizzle docs for exact syntax.

userStories.title: Add Loading and Error Boundaries
userStories.description: No loading.tsx or error.tsx files exist anywhere in the app. Server-rendered pages show nothing during navigation, and any server component error crashes the entire page with no recovery.
acceptanceCriteria: Create app/loading.tsx with a centered spinner matching the design system (use existing Tailwind animate-spin pattern from other components)
Create app/error.tsx as a client component ('use client') with a 'Something went wrong' message, a retry button that calls reset(), and a link back to dashboard. Use design system colors.
Create app/menus/[id]/loading.tsx with a skeleton showing the breadcrumb area, a large rectangle for PDF viewer, and a sidebar placeholder
Create app/settings/loading.tsx with a skeleton showing the tab bar and a content area placeholder
All loading/error files use the warm cream background (#FAF7F2) and design system colors
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Next.js App Router uses loading.tsx for Suspense boundaries during navigation and error.tsx for error boundaries. The dashboard (app/page.tsx), menu detail (app/menus/[id]/page.tsx), and settings (app/settings/page.tsx) are all server components that currently block the UI while fetching data.

userStories.title: Shared Date Formatting Utility
userStories.description: Date formatting is inconsistent across the codebase. Some components create Intl.DateTimeFormat outside the component (good), others inline it in render. Create a shared utility.
acceptanceCriteria: Create lib/format.ts with formatDate(date) returning 'DD MMM YYYY' format (e.g., '19 Jan 2026') using en-GB locale
Add formatDateTime(date) returning 'DD MMM YYYY, HH:MM' format (e.g., '19 Jan 2026, 14:30') using en-GB locale
Both functions accept Date or string input and handle null/undefined by returning an empty string
Replace inline Intl.DateTimeFormat usage in: app/menus/[id]/versions/[versionId]/page.tsx, components/menu-card.tsx, components/comments-list.tsx
Replace the hoisted dateFormatter in app/activity/page.tsx with the shared import
All replaced usages produce the same output format as before
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: Currently app/activity/page.tsx hoists: const dateFormatter = new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' }). The version detail page uses inline: new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-GB', { ... }).format(). Standardize to one import.

userStories.title: Convert New Menu Page to Server Component
userStories.description: app/menus/new/page.tsx is a client component that fetches categories and tags via useEffect on mount. Convert the data fetching to server-side and pass as props, matching the pattern used by the dashboard (app/page.tsx) and menu detail (app/menus/[id]/page.tsx).
acceptanceCriteria: app/menus/new/page.tsx becomes a server component that fetches categories and tags from DB directly (using db import from @/lib/db)
Server component checks auth with getCurrentUser() and redirects to /login if not authenticated
Server component passes categories and tags arrays as props to a new client component
Create components/new-menu-form.tsx as the client component ('use client') containing the form state and submission logic currently in the page
The new client component receives categories and tags as props instead of fetching them
No useEffect data fetching remains in the new menu flow
Form behavior (submission, validation, redirect) works identically to before
bun run build passes without errors
userStories.context: The current page is entirely 'use client' and fetches /api/categories and /api/tags in useEffect. This causes a loading waterfall: page loads -> JS executes -> two API calls -> render. Server-fetching eliminates the waterfall. Follow the exact pattern used in app/page.tsx where getMenusWithDetails() fetches data and passes it to DashboardFilters client component.
